title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 126.0930: retuned Markov headroom and floor on the 650-instruction R=2^20 package

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack described in proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^126.0930 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). The construction is the public 126.0931 package (736c001a): R=2^20 table, checkpoint-only cycle detection, rare-event field kernels (fe_mul 85, fe_sqr 64, plain fe_sub for x3/y3, failure rows 2^-62.4 and 2^-96), counted loops 105/468, ordinary step 650, doubling 797, traversal 674, kappa=1.01 H1. The only change is the retune of the two free ledger parameters: Markov headroom h=0.0001696 (was 0.000165) and floor p0=0.3901709 (was 0.3901753), giving p0 - h - 2e-7 = 0.3900011 > 0.390001 > 0.39. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: phase 1 = 2^126.0925192, hard extras = 2^111.8068074 (checkpoint writes 2^111.7482221), expected random extras = 2^101.7708998, allowance = ceil(extras/0.0001696) = 2^114.2964760, total W_ledger = 2^126.0929970 < 2^126.0930; the exact Markov ratio is 0.000168373 < 0.0001696. certificate.py proves the bound in exact integer and rational arithmetic, including W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1260930 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1260929. The claim is self-contained in proof.md; no prior acceptance, review verdict, official score or cross-submission comparison is a premise. The construction is credited as provenance and declared as a dependency on submission 736c001a. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break or executed production attack.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb-for-limb Python ports of the generated field kernels (asserting every no-overflow step and the rare-event predicates) checked against big integers and affine secp256k1, the shipped counted loops and emitter wrappers executed by an AArch64 interpreter (including constructed reduction inputs whose last addition carries, which must return the predicted z mod p - C0), instruction counts parsed from the shipped assembly, and the work-meter ledger recomputed from the prices and rows of proof.md. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
